create.title: Delta/Farey reduction to a short-numerator Kloosterman family
create.statement_tex: Let J=sqrt(X), T=J/Q, and let the fixed-interior signed product wavelet have K=hat(g) with g smooth, compactly supported, and separated from zero. Exact Poisson summation in the offset localizes the circle variable to ||alpha|| asymp T^(-1). Therefore a Farey dissection of order R<T/O(1), in particular R=Q at the benchmark, has only the 0/1 cell and is exactly the known two-dimensional Fourier self-return. At conductor order J, every nonzero contributing reduced fraction has T<<c<<J and b=min(a,c-a)<<c/T, so the actual numerator length is A_c asymp c/T<=Q and A_c<sqrt(c), the latter because c<=J<T^2 at the benchmark. The complete two-variable residue is an ordinary Kloosterman local factor for odd c and a conductor-4 twisted local factor for even c only after counterfactual numerator completion. Its double zero mode vanishes, but single-zero axial modes and gcd factors survive. Hence termwise completion plus Weil and standard complete-sum Kuznetsov do not prove the J^(1/2) target. The first open interface is the joint dyadic (c,b,dual-frequency) estimate with actual weights, which must save T/J^(1/2)=X^(1/20) at J=X^(1/2), Q=X^(1/5). This is a fixed-smooth-interior reduction/no-go and gives no full-cone or exponent estimate.
create.next_action: Prove a dyadic joint large-sieve bound for the actual incomplete numerator family c asymp C, b asymp c/T, including both even-modulus types, axial modes, gcds, and dual weights; do not complete b termwise or repeat the zero-cell Poisson return.

update.next_action: The natural delta cutoff is an exact zero-cell self-return; conductor scale exposes only an incomplete numerator c/T<sqrt(c). Prove the joint short-numerator/modulus estimate saving X^(1/20), or pivot to an independent blocker.
The delta method at natural cutoff returns exactly to this wavelet; at conductor scale its only new form is a joint short-numerator Kloosterman family. Attack that family without termwise completion.
Exact circle localization confirms the product-wavelet self-return. Any improvement now requires joint cancellation in the incomplete numerator/modulus family, not another one-variable transform.

The delta/Kloosterman reformulation retains the same H/L-sized deficit in a short moving numerator. Standard complete-sum estimates do not prove PSC; a genuinely joint signed near-product theorem remains necessary.

reject.reason: After the signed offset Poisson transform, the circle support lies inside the 0/1 Farey cell whenever R<T/O(1), including the natural R=Q cutoff.
The actual numerator has length c/T<sqrt(c), so completing it and applying a square-root complete-sum bound is non-improving.
Standard Kuznetsov averages complete Kloosterman sums over moduli; completing the actual numerator creates about T moving arguments and does not preserve the required power.
For odd c the counterfactually completed numerator is an ordinary Kloosterman sum; the chi_4-twisted or Salié-type factors occur only in the even-modulus cases.
The double zero mode vanishes, but odd-c rho=0 and 4|c sigma=0 axial modes survive, including Ramanujan or twisted-Gauss gcd degenerations.
A single congruence also counts nonzero aliases mn-N-s=lc; exact circle or delta-symbol weights are mandatory.

no_change.reason: The signed short-numerator estimate, cone edges, remaining radial sectors, and endpoint completion remain open.
Both M9-M1 and M9-M2 remain open.
Round 70 proves a reduction/no-go but no new target-sized estimate or exponent.

round_assessment.reason: Round 70 rigorously reconciles the natural and conductor delta cutoffs, computes the exact residue families and zero modes, and isolates a narrower joint incomplete-numerator estimate while proving that completion, Weil, and standard Kuznetsov do not supply the missing X^(1/20).
